To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cobalt promotes small diameter CNTs, Nickel promotes the best quality CNTs, Iron promotes low yielding and Mo promotes low quality CNTs.
the CNTs structures obtained with Ni and Co are more efficient than Fe or Mo.
the type of metal catalyst has a significant effect on the morphology of the CNTs, with cobalt promoting the best results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the effect of the catalysts in the production of CNTs, in the aim of finding a catalyst that promotes the production of high quality CNTs.
the synthesis and characterization of carbon nanotube (CNTs) structures by chemical vapour deposition process.
the development of an automatized process, which is capable to produce CNTs using methane as carbon source and different transition metal catalysts, such as Ni, Co, Fe and Mo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ni is the catalyst with the highest efficiency for growing CNTs with a high quality.
Ni is the best catalyst for the synthesis of high quality carbon nanotubes, with a good efficiency, and Co is the second best.
Co is the best catalyst for the synthesis of high quality and high yield of CNTs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CNTs synthesis process is highly dependent on the metal type and the metal loading.
the best catalyst for CNTs production with methane would be Ni, followed by Co, Mo and Fe.
the use of Co and Ni nanoparticles as catalyst for CVD process is more efficient and less expensive than the use of Fe or Mo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CVD process can be used for CNTs growing using methane as carbon source.
the catalyst plays a crucial role in the production of carbon nanotube, and it is possible to produce high quality CNTs with low cost and high efficiency.
